title: Regular affine Koszul comparisons natural under nested charts
statement: For a closed immersion i:Z→Y, an arbitrary open V of Z and n≥0, use B,S,H,G,T,F as in the compatible-cover statement. No regularity assumption is made on V. For every affine U of Y whose immersion ideal admits finite Koszul-regular generators, there are simultaneous isomorphisms F.over(V⁻¹(i⁻¹U)) ≅ T.over(V⁻¹(i⁻¹U)). If U0⊆U1 are two such regular affine charts, their hom components agree on every subopen of V⁻¹(i⁻¹U0). No compatibility of nonnested charts or point-indexed cover is asserted.

proof.text: Obtain a global exterior-to-self-Tor morphism tau with chartwise invertible dual, and a global self-Ext-to-dual-self-Tor morphism epsilon with chartwise invertibility. On V set phi=restrict(epsilon) followed by restrict(dualMap(tau)): T -> F. The over functor maps this composition to the composite of two isomorphisms on every regular affine chart.

Index regular affine charts by the subtype of affine opens together with the stated existence of regular generators. For each chart take the inverse of asIso(phi.over chart), yielding the required F.over chart -> T.over chart isomorphism. All choices occur inside the theorem proof; no data definition is chosen from an existence theorem.

Prove compatibility by evaluating the inverse equations on any common subopen A. Write f for the component of the one global phi and g_j,g_k for two chartwise inverse components. Then g_j followed by f is the identity and f followed by g_k is the identity. Associativity gives g_j = g_j followed by (f followed by g_k) = (g_j followed by f) followed by g_k = g_k. This works even without nesting, and in particular proves the required nested compatibility.

lean.statement:
theorem koszulRegularImmersion_self_ext_conormal_nested_charts
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (V : Z.Opens) (n : ℕ) :
    let B := (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)
    let S := DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let G := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) (n : ℤ)).obj
        (H.obj (op (S.obj B), S.obj B))
    let T := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj G)
    let F := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      (Scheme.Modules.dual (Scheme.Modules.exteriorSheaf
        ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules) n))
    ∃ c : ∀ (U : Y.affineOpens)
      (_hU : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U.1)),
        Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U ∧
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f),
        F.over (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)) ≅ T.over (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)),
      ∀ (U₀ U₁ : Y.affineOpens)
        (h₀ : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U₀.1)),
          Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U₀ ∧
            RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f)
        (h₁ : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → Γ(Y, U₁.1)),
          Ideal.span (Set.range f) = i.ker.ideal U₁ ∧
            RingTheory.Sequence.IsKoszulRegular f)
        (_h : U₀.1 ≤ U₁.1) (A : V.toScheme.Opens)
        (hA₀ : A ≤ V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U₀.1))
        (hA₁ : A ≤ V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U₁.1)),
        (c U₀ h₀).hom.val.app (op (Over.mk (homOfLE hA₀))) =
          (c U₁ h₁).hom.val.app (op (Over.mk (homOfLE hA₁)))
